clue.text: Religious leader muffles anguished cries of overseer

indicators.note: to muffle something is to wrap it up, so the leader encloses the other letters

parts.note: the head of the Roman Catholic Church

indicators.note: anguished cries are twisted and contorted, so the following word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleric stifles the howls of a supervisor in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: Overseer looks like a person in charge, but it is a device for seeing over things, as from a submerged submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's sighting tube lets its user look over obstacles, a playful sense of someone who oversees.

clue.text: Gradually destroy heartless expensive nursing staff

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the outer letters cradle the other piece
with its heart gone, only the two ends of the next word survive

parts.note: just the first and last letters of the word
a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: Costly nurses are cruelly wearing down the hospital team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursing staff' looks like hospital workers, but nursing is the container signal and staff is just a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear something away bit by bit, as water does rock.

clue.text: Motivation provided by setter's favourite American

parts.note: the setter speaks of himself as I, so setter's is I'M, I am
a teacher's pet is the favourite
standard abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: The compiler claims his drive comes from a beloved American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' stands for I'M, the setter saying 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or drive that gets something moving, a close synonym of motivation.

clue.text: Arrive on time to see heavenly body

parts.note: to arrive is to come
T is the physics symbol for time, placed on the end

explanation.surface: Turn up punctually to watch something in the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy object orbiting the sun with a glowing tail, one of the bodies seen in the sky.

clue.text: See 8
Gemstone and silver put away

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
to put food away is to eat it

explanation.surface: Jewels and silverware are stored safely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' looks like storing the valuables, but it is the informal sense of eating, so ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded variety of chalcedony cut and polished as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Missile thrown by German soldiers destroyed Dane

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the name is reassembled in another order

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bomb hurled by German troops kills a Danish man.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a common crossword source of 'soldiers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small explosive bomb thrown by hand, so it is a type of missile.

clue.text: Old penny turned up in channel for milk in drinks dispenser

indicators.note: these letters go inside the following channel

parts.note: the nipple through which milk passes to the young

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning letters upward makes them read from bottom to top

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: An ancient coin has surfaced in a milk duct inside a vending machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old penny' looks like one thing, such as D, but it splits into O and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapot holds brewed tea and pours it out into cups, a humble dispenser of drinks.

clue.text: Nick has almost clean cut of meat

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: clean and pure are synonyms
a loin is a joint of meat from the back

explanation.surface: A man named Nick owns a nearly spotless joint from the butcher.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a man's name, but it is the slang verb meaning to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nick and purloin are verbs for stealing, nick being British slang.

clue.text: Setter finally meeting old politician for sexy fun

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the preceding word

parts.note: the last letter of the word
O is the abbreviation for old
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: The compiler at last hooks up with a retired MP for a frolic.
explanation.definitionFit: A romp is light-hearted frolicking, and in British tabloid usage a sexual escapade.

clue.text: Encountered silence about beer rejected for large bottle of wine

parts.note: to encounter is to meet, past tense met

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for silence wraps the other piece

parts.note: hush and silence are synonyms

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker turned down beer in favour of a big bottle of wine and met with silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A methuselah is a champagne or wine bottle holding eight standard bottles, named after the long-lived biblical patriarch.

clue.text: Price paid by Trotsky's first supporters?

parts.note: a fee is a charge paid

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the name is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: It reads like a political question: what did Trotsky's followers pay?
explanation.walkthrough: Trotsky's supporters suggest followers of the revolutionary, but the definition is a whimsical one, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Your feet hold your body up, so they literally support you, a playful sense of supporters.

clue.text: Turned-on bird badly disrupted date

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An aroused girl spoiled a romantic evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is British slang for a young woman, which helps the surface, but here it is a real bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite, especially sexually, so titillated means aroused or turned on.

clue.text: Sign outside hospital found by a body part

indicators.note: outside means the sign wraps around the letter for hospital

parts.note: a trace is a sign or mark left behind
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a severed limb by a hospital signpost.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the tube carrying air from the throat to the lungs.

clue.text: Guard ignoring Southern door

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so that letter goes

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A sentry on duty overlooks the south gate.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is a way in, such as a door or doorway into a building.

clue.text: Commune dismissing Tory's literary offering

indicators.note: to dismiss someone is to send them away, so that word leaves the longer one

parts.note: to commune is to talk intimately, or converse
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A hippie community throws out a Conservative's poetry submission.
explanation.walkthrough: Commune looks like a noun for a hippie collective, but it is the verb meaning to talk. Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is poetry, a piece of writing one might offer as a literary contribution.

clue.text: Steer clear of notorious fruit picker eating apple dishes for starters

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the picker swallows the other letters

parts.note: in Genesis Eve picked the forbidden fruit

indicators.note: starters are the first parts, so the opening letters of the two words are used

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Avoid the infamous orchard worker who eats apple dishes as appetisers.
explanation.walkthrough: Starters looks like a meal course alongside dishes, but it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to avoid or escape something, which is to steer clear of it.

clue.text: Communist leader adopting finest revised set of political proposals

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the leader's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Mao Zedong, leader of Communist China

indicators.note: a revised text is reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mao takes up the best ideas and reworks them into a party programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published declaration of a party's policies and aims.

clue.text: Mates pass away surrounded by flowers

indicators.note: the phrase puts the word for passing away inside the word for flowers

parts.note: buds are unopened flowers
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: Friends die at peace amid floral tributes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mates and buddies are both informal words for close friends.

clue.text: Concern about texture of ornamental tablet

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for concern wraps the other word

parts.note: care and concern are synonyms
the touch of a fabric is its texture or feel

explanation.surface: Worry over the feel of a decorated slab.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche is a carved scroll-shaped panel or tablet, often framing an inscription, like the oval rings of Egyptian hieroglyphs.

clue.text: Slaughter big cat beneath walls of tower

indicators.note: walls enclose a building, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
the ounce is the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A big cat kills prey below a castle's battlements.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, beneath means the cat comes after the tower's walls. Slaughter here is the sporting sense of beating someone heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to defeat decisively, as a team slaughters its opponents in a one-sided game.

clue.text: South American worker leaving despot for oversexed fellow

indicators.note: the worker leaves, so those letters are taken away from the tyrant word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
A is the abbreviation for American
a despot is a tyrant
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A Latin American labourer escapes a dictator to join a lecher.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth satyrs were lustful woodland creatures, so the word now describes a lecherous man.

clue.text: One pointing the finger with a chapter about addict

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for chapter
c is short for circa, Latin for about
a drug user is an addict

explanation.surface: Someone blaming an addict cites a passage from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: About looks like a container signal, but it is just C, for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: To point the finger is to blame someone, and an accuser is a person who lays the blame.

clue.text: Used part of watch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: owned previously by someone else
second meaning: the pointer that sweeps round marking seconds

explanation.surface: It reads like a note about a worn timepiece component.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an adjective for pre-owned goods and also names the thin pointer counting seconds on a dial.

clue.text: Dull chap in dull church

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour; this is the second dull, the one inside the clue
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A boring man sits in a drab church.
explanation.walkthrough: In looks like a container signal, but it only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow-witted person, the pupil once made to wear a pointed cap.

clue.text: Cold boy gets dressed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A chilly youngster puts his clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is an old past participle of clothe, meaning wearing clothes.

clue.text: See 30
Upset as noose traps swan when hunting rules are relaxed

indicators.note: a trap catches and holds something inside it
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A snare catching a swan is disturbing, now that hunting restrictions are eased.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan; the male is a cob.
explanation.definitionFit: The open season is the period of the year when it is legal to hunt or catch a given species.

clue.text: Handy suggestion about small and very good place where car can be serviced

definitions.text: place where car can be serviced

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tip is a useful hint
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
top means excellent

explanation.surface: Practical advice on finding a small, excellent garage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit stop is the halt in a motor race where the car is refuelled and repaired, and the area it happens in.

clue.text: Look into bishop's office before a match

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese or seat of authority
taken as written
a bout is a boxing or wrestling match

explanation.surface: Peek inside the bishop's study ahead of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To see about something is to deal with it or investigate, much as one would look into a matter.

clue.text: See 29
Expensive pickle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: unreasonably high in price
second meaning: to soak food in liquid, as in a marinade

explanation.definitionFit: The word means overpriced as an adjective and, as a verb, to soak something in liquid, which is how pickling works.

clue.text: Spoil hybrid seed container

indicators.note: a hybrid is a crossbreed, so the letters are mixed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a crate is a box for transporting goods

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that a crossbred seed tray has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: To desecrate is to violate something sacred, a strong way of spoiling or defiling it.
